newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries up in London as barrage of data looms.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries up in London as barrage of data looms.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ploughed ahead in London on Monday but a week full of weighty economic numbers should curb excessive movement this session, traders said.

"We're the tiniest bit better. We have a lovely week of statistics to look forward to -- employment cost, GDP, and of course the finale on Friday," said a trader at a U.S. bank here, referring to payroll data.
"I think we should be in a relatively narrow, possibly subdued trading range until then," he said.
The long bond was quoted at 99-13 at 1031 GMT, yielding 6.795 percent, up from 99-06 in Tokyo and 99-05 in New York.
December T-bond futures were quoted at 111-03, up 3/32 in automated trade from the pit settlement in Chicago on Friday.

There were no major data scheduled for release on Monday but Tuesday brings the employment cost index, Wednesday sees preliminary third quarter GDP, Thursday has personal income and spending and October payrolls cap the week on Friday.

"There's a very large stream of data coming in but I think the market will probably ignore most of it to look particularly at the non-farm payrolls," said Francesco Giordano, senior economist at San Paolo Bank in London.

He said the market had become slightly concerned that weekly jobless claims may point to a strong payroll number. At the same time, the General Motors Corp strike in Canada appears to have had little impact on GM's factories in the U.S., so the market cannot look for any relief on jobs growth there.

"We may see some weakness ahead of the employment data," he said. "Otherwise, the dollar has been reasonably supported and dollar/yen is looking very strong which might encourage some Japanese investment."
